paras: The mob hanging of Ilen Pettis took place in White County, Arkansas, in late December 1881, when ten masked men took Pettis, a Black prisoner accused of robbery, from jail and hanged him from a tree limb until he confessed. The men returned him alive to the jailer and handed the recovered money to the sheriff. It is known only from one Chicago Tribune dispatch, which reported it approvingly.

Samuel Waters, a planter who had recently moved from Woodruff County to Rosebud in White County, was travelling with money from a land sale. According to the dispatch, a man described as "a negro" struck him down by the road and robbed him. After a search, Pettis was arrested and jailed with a $100 Confederate bill, several $10 bills and silver, though most of the money was missing.

On the night after Pettis was jailed, ten masked men surrounded the jail and forced the jailer to lead them to his cell. They took him to woods some distance from town and told him his life would be spared only if he led them to the rest of the money. When he denied it, they put a rope around his neck, threw it over a limb, and drew him up and let him down three times.

The dispatch says Pettis then confessed and led the men to the rest of the money, hidden under a log in a thicket. The men returned him to the jailer, woke Sheriff Black, gave him the money for Waters, and "rode silently away."
Waters was reported to be in "a very critical condition" from his head wounds.

The only known account ran in the Chicago Daily Tribune on December 31, 1881, as a Little Rock special dispatch dated the day before. Under the headline "A ROBBER'S EXPERIENCE," it treated the confession as proof of guilt, called Pettis "the miserable wretch," and described the masked men's work without criticism. It named neither the men, their race, nor the town where the jail stood. No second report of the episode, in Arkansas or elsewhere, appears in the coverage.

accounts.label: Little Rock special dispatch
accounts.gist: Pettis, arrested for robbing Waters, was taken from jail by ten masked men, hanged up three times in the woods until he confessed, led them to the money and was returned to jail; the dispatch gives the band's results as proof of guilt.

framing.detail: Headline 'A ROBBER'S EXPERIENCE' and the phrase 'the miserable wretch' present Pettis as the guilty thief and the band's torture as a successful recovery of stolen money, with no criticism.
